title: low-aftermath
label: Jason Warrior

won.source: the fed's own bio card for Jason Warrior (cgi-bin/superstars.cgi?jasonwarrior), "LOW Aftermath Champion (June 11, 2003 to August 31, 2003 - Relinquished)"

how: Won on the fed's own first-anniversary pay-per-view, In The End, and relinquished rather than lost on the night of Wakeup Call.
note: The fed's own champion banner brackets this reign without reaching inside it: eleven captures between 17 April and 25 May 2003 show Iron Lung as Aftermath Champion, and the next capture that names the belt at all, 28 March 2004, names Tyrone Johnson. The fed's own served Realm 29 of 8 April 2003 bills Iron Lung "the Aftermath Champion" and calls the belt "his newly won Aftermath Championship", which places the end of his own undated reign after that date and before this one begins.

title: low-world
label: Annihilation

won.source: The fed's own served CATASTROPHIC pay-per-view, on which the belt changes hands.

how: Won the Asylum Match over Eric Russo, Luke Justice and Mike Meyhu. The change is declared narratively rather than by the ring announcer: the bell sounds, "the referee is seen raising the hand of a fallen Annihilation", and in the segment that follows he unhooks the belt from the wire lowering it into the cage and puts it round his waist.
note: In the same segment as the win, the fed staged Annihilation hanging himself on the wire that lowered the belt, and The fed's own champion banner — a strip of champion portraits it stamped into the masthead of every page, each carrying the belt and the holder in its own image title — shows the World Championship VACANT on captures of 8 December 2004, six weeks later. The reign is recorded as vacated on that evidence; the fed's own record does not date the vacancy.
